methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements that capture a single aspect of the timer's functionality or implementation. The goal was to create a set of atomic units that could be easily compared and analyzed for coverage and similarity.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Implement a timer.
Timer counts down for a given number of clock cycles.
Timer asserts a signal when the duration has elapsed.
Use a down-counter to implement the timer.
Down-counter asserts an output signal when the count becomes 0.
If load = 1, load the internal counter with the 10-bit data.
10-bit data represents the number of clock cycles to count.
Counter can be loaded at any time, including when it is still counting.
Loading the counter will immediately update the counter's value
Loading the counter will de-assert the tc signal
If load = 0 and the internal counter is greater than 0, the internal counter should decrement by 1.
If load = 0 and the internal counter is already at 0, the internal counter should remain at 0.
Output signal tc indicates whether the internal counter has reached 0.
Once the internal counter has reached 0, it should stay 0 (stop counting).
output signal 'tc' should remain asserted until the counter is loaded again.
When the counter is loaded again, 'tc' should de-assert.
clk is an input
load is an input
data is an input
tc is an output
spec_atomic_units: The output 'tc' is asserted when the internal counter reaches zero.
tc remains asserted until the 'data' input is loaded again via the 'load' signal.
The combinational logic determines the value of 'tc' based on the current state of the counter and the 'load' signal.
If the counter value is zero, 'tc' is 1.
Otherwise, 'tc' is 0.
The comparison of the 10-bit counter value to zero is the core combinational logic function.
The 'load' signal does not directly affect the combinational logic that determines 'tc'.
The combinational logic is solely responsible for detecting the zero condition of the counter.
The combinational logic within the `top_module` is responsible for generating the `tc` (terminal count) output signal.
The `tc` output is asserted (set to 1) if and only if the 10-bit counter value is equal to zero.
Otherwise, `tc` is de-asserted (set to 0).
The `load` input does not directly influence the combinational logic that generates `tc`.
The combinational logic block can be described as a zero-detection circuit.
This circuit takes the 10-bit counter value as input and produces a single-bit output (`tc`).
The zero-detection can be implemented using a 10-input NOR gate.
The inputs to the NOR gate are the individual bits of the counter.
If all bits of the counter are zero, the output of the NOR gate (i.e., `tc`) will be one.
Otherwise, the output will be zero.
`tc = ~(counter[9] | counter[8] | counter[7] | counter[6] | counter[5] | counter[4] | counter[3] | counter[2] | counter[1] | counter[0])`.
The counter value is an input to the combinational logic, even though it is derived from sequential logic.
The combinational logic block continuously monitors the counter value and updates the `tc` output accordingly.
The `load` signal only affects the sequential logic that updates the counter value and does not directly influence the combinational logic that generates `tc`.
The module `top_module` implements a timer that counts down from a loaded value and asserts a terminal count (tc) signal when the count reaches zero.
The timer can be reloaded at any time.
The `clk` input is the clock signal.
The `load` input, when high, causes the internal counter to be loaded with the value from the `data` input.
The `data` input provides the 10-bit initial count value.
The `tc` output is asserted when the internal counter reaches zero.
When `load` is asserted, the counter is immediately loaded with `data` and `tc` is de-asserted.
When `load` is de-asserted, the counter decrements on each rising edge of `clk` if the counter is greater than 0.
Once the counter reaches 0, it remains at 0 and `tc` remains asserted until `load` is asserted again.
The counter's value updates on the rising edge of `clk`.
The `tc` output is dependent on the current value of the internal counter.
When `load` is asserted, the counter updates immediately, and `tc` is de-asserted.
When `load` is de-asserted, the counter decrements on each rising edge of `clk` if the counter is greater than 0.
There is a one clock cycle delay between the counter decrementing and the `tc` output potentially changing.
This is a sequential circuit with one 10-bit register to store the counter value.
The register updates on the rising edge of the `clk` signal.
A non-blocking assignment (`<=`) is used to update the register's value.
The `tc` output is a combinational function of the register's value.
The register is loaded with `data` when `load` is high.
When `load` is low and the counter is greater than 0, the register decrements.
When the counter is 0, it remains at 0.
